title: thermal-horizon-rar: Testing the Thermal-Horizon Reading of the Radial Acceleration Relation, from Galaxies to Wide Binaries
description: Measurement and theory-testing program for gravity at low accelerations, deposited as a complete repository snapshot: coefficient-level tests of the radial acceleration relation on SPARC rotation curves and KiDS-1000 lensing data; a joint two-dimensional (velocity, direction-angle) likelihood measurement of the low-acceleration velocity boost in 14,071 Gaia EDR3 wide binaries, with completeness marginalization, seed and bootstrap error budgets, and a noise-ceiling profile; the solar-system quadrupole consequences of the measured amplitude; a modified-inertia versus modified-gravity discrimination on the binary data; a reconciliation by ablation of the conflicting published wide-binary analyses; a Hubble-constant meter built from the a0-to-H0 inversion on distance-independent SPARC rotation curves; and a horizon-thermal mechanism programme with its exact results, its exclusions, and its open constants. Four manuscripts are under papers/ (wide binaries; radial-acceleration-relation coefficients; the Hubble meter; mechanism); the citable archived PDFs are at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22050990 (the first two) and doi:10.5281/zenodo.22923373 (the Hubble meter). The frozen internal record is PAPER.md; the chronological lab notebook, including every correction and retraction, is NOTES-horizon-inertia.md; the curated measurement ledger is LEDGER.csv; signed predictions registered before test are in PREDICTIONS.md. Every claimed number is reproduced by a named script under calcs/, every analysis stage was pre-registered in a commit made before the run, calcs/fetch_inputs.py retrieves and hash-verifies the input data in one command, and REPRO.md walks the full reproduction path.
